sections.h2: Where do Coweta County owners take property tax questions?
sections.html:
Bills and payments go through the Tax Commissioner at 87 Newnan Station Drive, Suite 100, Newnan, GA 30265. Valuation and homestead decisions go through the Assessor's Office at 37 Perry Street in Newnan. Phone numbers are 770-254-2670 for the commissioner and 770-254-2680 for the assessors.

The commissioner's counter keeps weekday hours of 8:00am to 4:30pm. The tax commissioner's site adds that the Board of County Commissioners and the Board of Education each set a millage rate, and the grand jury appoints the board that hears disputes. If you need a copy of your deed, the Clerk of Superior Court sits at the Coweta County Justice Center, 72 Greenville Street, Newnan, and the commissioner's FAQ lists 770-254-2690 for that office.

  • Value or exemption: Assessor's Office.
  • Bill, payoff or lien: Tax Commissioner.
  • Deed copy: Clerk of Superior Court.

sections.h2: What is Coweta County like for someone preparing to sell?
sections.html:
Coweta County is a Piedmont county in West Central Georgia that belongs to the Atlanta metro area, and Newnan serves as both seat and largest city. The Georgia legislature drew its lines on June 9, 1826 after the Creek cession, and the county takes its name from the Koweta people.

Cities include Newnan, Senoia, Grantville, Palmetto and Chattahoochee Hills, and the towns are Haralson, Moreland, Sharpsburg and Turin. Palmetto and Chattahoochee Hills spill over the Fulton County line. An odd piece of local land history is Shenandoah, a 7,400-acre federally backed planned town begun in the early 1970s and foreclosed on in 1981. Wikipedia places the eastern half of the county in the Upper Flint River basin and the western half in the Lake Harding stretch of the Chattahoochee basin.

Population climbed from 127,317 in 2010 to 146,158 in 2020, and QuickFacts counts 160,240 as of July 2025. Census five-year estimates give owned homes a typical value of $357,500 and an owner-occupancy rate of 78.4%. Gross rent is $1,488, household income is $95,548, and workers spend an average of 29.8 minutes getting to their jobs.

sections.h2: What does the Coweta County tax calendar look like?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed October 1 and come due December 1, according to the commissioner's site. It adds that mailing happens at least 60 days ahead, and that your printed bill is the authority if the date shifts.

The building has a drive-up drop box, and online card payments carry a convenience fee collected by the card company. Mailed checks need a postmark that is no later than the due date. When December 1 lands on a day the office is closed, payment is accepted the next business day.

  • January 1: who owned and used the property fixes the year's tax.
  • Through April 1: the filing window for returns and first-year homestead or special program applications.
  • April 1: mobile and manufactured home tax is due, and the location decal follows payment.
  • October 1: bills mailed.
  • December 1: land, building and personal property tax due.

sections.h2: What does Coweta County charge on late bills?
sections.html:
The commissioner's pages give a three-part answer: interest at the bank prime loan rate plus 3% each month, a 5% penalty once 120 days have passed, and another 5% every 120 days after that up to a 20% ceiling. Homesteaded property with a bill under $500 does not take the penalty.

A FiFa lien is recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court when a bill stays unpaid, and the FAQ places that at more than 30 days after the due date. The lien stays on a credit record for a minimum of seven years. The office mails delinquent notices only at intervals, so it tells owners to confirm the amount due before paying.

Mobile and manufactured homes face a different consequence: a 10% penalty, a citation to Coweta County State Court, or even sale of the home if the April 1 payment and permit are missed.

sections.h2: Who pays the Coweta County tax when a house changes hands?
sections.html:
Whoever owned on January 1 is the name on the lien. The commissioner says a seller who gets a bill after selling should pass it to the buyer, but the lien only moves if the office is shown a contract or closing statement by day 90 after the due date.

That means a seller whose closing prorated the tax should carry the settlement statement to Newnan Station Drive. If the office receives it and the bill stays unpaid, the lien is recorded against the new owner.

Timing helps here. Because bills are mailed in October, a spring or summer closing usually happens before that year's bill exists, so the title company has to estimate. Request the prior year's total from the commissioner as a benchmark, and ask the closer to explain how the estimate was set.

sections.h2: What are the three ways to appeal in Coweta County?
sections.html:
Owners get 45 days from the assessment notice, and the first step is a written appeal filed with the Board of Assessors on the state's uniform form, naming the method you prefer. The grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

Appeal routes the Coweta County Tax Commissioner describes
RouteBest suited toWhat follows
Board of EqualizationMost homeownersHearing, then Superior Court if needed
Hearing officerNon-homestead real property valued at $1,000,000 or moreDecision, then Superior Court if needed
ArbitrationOwners holding a current certified appraisalHearing within 30 days; the ruling is final

Under the first route, the assessors may revise the value and mail a new notice, which you can appeal within 30 days. An appeal they leave unchanged is forwarded on its own to the equalization board for a hearing. Arbitration requires the assessors to acknowledge the appeal within 45 days, and if they reject your appraisal they must certify the case to the Clerk of Superior Court.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special programs apply in Coweta County?
sections.html:
A homestead claim requires owning and living in the house on January 1, and the application must arrive by April 1 of the first year. Late filings roll forward a year. The assessors make the final call, you may not claim a homestead anywhere else, and a denial can be appealed.

Coweta County has its own local exemptions that replace the state figure when larger. The assessors will explain what proof they need for age, income or military service. After approval, the exemption renews without a new application until you move or the owner changes.

  • Tax deferral for owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less, lasting until a change of ownership or until the balance and interest reach 85% of fair market value.
  • Agricultural assessment at 30% of fair market value for qualifying farmland.
  • Conservation Use and Forest Land Protection, with covenants of 10 or 15 years.
  • Historic property and Hazardous Site Reuse preferential assessment.

The special programs must be applied for in the first four months of the year they begin. A buyer of an enrolled tract should ask the assessors whether the covenant carries over to the new owner.

faqs.q: Which office in Coweta County sends my property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Tax Commissioner, at 87 Newnan Station Drive, Suite 100, Newnan. Bills go out October 1, and you can call 770-254-2670.

faqs.q: Is December 1 the Coweta County due date for every bill?
faqs.a: For land, buildings and personal property, yes, per the commissioner's site. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1, and the printed bill states the date that applies to you.

faqs.q: Can a hearing officer decide my Coweta County homestead appeal?
faqs.a: No. The county limits hearing officers to disputes over the value of non-homestead real property worth $1,000,000 or more.

faqs.q: Where do I get my deed in Coweta County?
faqs.a: From the Clerk of Superior Court at the Coweta County Justice Center, 72 Greenville Street, Newnan, GA 30263. The commissioner's FAQ gives 770-254-2690 for the clerk.

faqs.q: Do Coweta County penalties apply to every unpaid bill?
faqs.a: Not to homesteaded property with a bill under $500. Other unpaid bills take the 5% penalty after 120 days, repeating every 120 days up to a 20% cap.
